findings.title: rclone stderr is merged into the JSON that is parsed as the rule list
findings.description: `RULES=$(RCLONE_B2_ACCOUNT=… rclone backend lifecycle ":b2:$BUCKET" 2>&1)` captures stderr together with stdout so the failure text can be printed on a real failure (good), but it also means a successful `rclone` run that emits any warning line to stderr will fail the `jq -e 'type == "array"'` gate and be reported as `UNREADABLE lifecycle (not a JSON rule list: …)` — a false "cannot read" on a healthy bucket. The message does include the offending text, so the failure is diagnosable, and the whole item is read-only either way; worth considering capturing stdout and stderr separately (e.g. `2 > >(cat >&2)`-style split or a temp file) if rclone ever gets chatty.

findings.title: run_lib's fallback error line names `env`, not the library that failed
findings.description: When a prefixed library call fails without printing a DRIFT/MISSING/PENDING line, `report "MISSING ${prefix:+$prefix }$(basename "$1") exited $rc"` evaluates `basename` of `env` (the first remaining argument after `shift`, since the call is `run_lib "$C" env PGCLUSTER=… pg_settings.sh …`), producing e.g. `MISSING 17/tick env exited 1` instead of naming `pg_settings.sh`. The pre-227 call had the same shape (empty prefix, `MISSING env exited …`), so this is carried-over cosmetic drift in the failure path, not a regression; fixing it would mean resolving the last `$1` or passing the library path explicitly.

findings.title: tick advisory-lock guard is check-then-act with an inherent race window
findings.description: `tick_locks_held()` is re-checked immediately before `systemctl restart postgresql@17-tick`, but a tick ingestion run can acquire its advisory lock between the check and the restart; the window is small and the same check-then-restart shape is what the slice design (TD6) specifies, and recovery is "fix the cause, re-run" — but it is a TOCTOU by construction, worth remembering if tick runs ever become continuous rather than timer-fired.

findings.title: Test coverage is exemplary and follows the project's conventions
findings.description: The suite runs the pure helpers against the real rendered cron file (produced by invoking `render_cron.sh` for real) and the real pre-227 installed-file fixture; host calls are replaced at module level; the setup-backup tests stub `pg_lsclusters` with the real tool's observed output shape and stub `rclone` to prove the lifecycle check never issues a mutating call; the provisioner tests extract and execute the script's own `hba_content()` rather than re-spelling it. Edge cases (malformed table, missing pgdata, pending restart on production, held lock, WAL timeout, unreadable rules, same-day re-run) are all parametrized or explicit. No gaps found on the critical paths reviewed.
